prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in League City, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1143; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where the accident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane road in League City, Texas, near a shopping center. I was moving over to get into the right lane.
Q: What time of day was it, and what were the road conditions like?
A: It was in the afternoon. It was dry, traffic was moderate, and the sun was pretty bright, so I had to squint a little.
Q: Walk me through what happened when you changed lanes.
A: I checked my mirror, saw a gap, and signaled. As I started to move over, I felt a bump on my driver's side and heard scraping. The other car had come up alongside me in the lane I was entering.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you started to move?
A: Not that I can remember clearly. I think it was in my blind spot. I checked the mirror, but I didn't turn my head to look over my shoulder before I merged. I probably should have.
Q: Did you or the other driver stop afterward?
A: Yes, we both pulled onto the shoulder. We exchanged insurance information and took a few photos of the damage.
Q: Did you notice any injuries at the scene?
A: Not right away. I was a bit shaken up, but I didn't think it was serious. Later that evening my lower back started to tighten up and it's gotten worse since.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment for your back?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They said it was a muscle strain and gave me some medication and told me to rest and do stretching exercises.
Q: Are you still experiencing pain or limitations?
A: Yes, sitting for long periods is hard, and I've had to take time off from lifting at work. I'm still going to physical therapy twice a week.
Q: Is there anything else you think is important for me to know?
A: Just that I'm willing to cooperate and provide the medical records you need.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
